author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts) with in-force catalog patterns only. The small adjustment has three parts. (1) SpecialtyRepository is a second Spring Data repository in vet/. It is needed because only the specialties table knows an unheld specialty, and VetRepository cannot list it. Its precedent is PetTypeRepository for a lookup value (grep-resolved: owner/PetTypeRepository.java; no IDE oracle connected, so grep is the weaker basis). (2) SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Value object; § Domain Core closed properties apply in full, and the entity exception does not cover it). It inverts vet-to-specialty into specialty-to-vets. The inversion lives here and not in the controller, per the Web controller row, which admits no business rule. (3) SpecialtyController serves GET /specialties.html with template vets/specialtyList.html, one controller per surface as in § Naming. VetRepository.findAll() (cached) supplies the veterinarians. Specialty gains no inverse association (system-design § Contracts invariants). Design-doc write: Contracts rows for the three new types, and REQ-VET-003 joined to Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository, plus a package-line and invariants sentence.
integration_points: Binding: SpecialtyController GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter and no request-bound type. It needs no @InitBinder. Adding any parameter later brings the identifier disallow list (security-principles, Mass assignment row).

Double, domain grouping: SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses real Vet and Specialty objects with ids set via setId. No double is needed. It covers all five acceptance behaviors, including the unheld specialty, which the seed data cannot show because every seeded specialty is held.

Double, repository boundary plus framework transport: SpecialtyControllerTests drives MockMvc (the sanctioned transport stand-in, testing-principles § Mocking Policy) over real repositories on the embedded H2 seed data (@SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc). Seeded Helen Leary under radiology and James Carter under none give the full-name and no-specialty assertions. A @MockitoBean repository stub is not sanctioned for this slice; if a web-slice test is preferred, use hand-written repository doubles.

Layout: the page uses fragments/layout with a menu name that matches no nav entry. The site navigation still renders (REQ-SYS-001), no entry is highlighted, and layout.html gains no link (PRD non-goal).

Messages: reuse the existing keys where they fit (specialties, vets, name). Any new key goes into all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002, enforced by I18nPropertiesSyncTest). No literal wording in the template.

patterns.description: repository for a persisted lookup value; name-ordered JPQL is the model for SpecialtyRepository
table rendering and full-name composition firstName + ' ' + lastName; the specialty directory omits the pagination block
constructor-injected repository, Model attributes, view-name return; a separate controller for the new surface

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, and Specialty instances from SpecialtyRepository and from a cached Vet are different objects. Grouping by object identity or a Set/Map keyed on Specialty would silently list every specialty with no veterinarians.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory matches specialties by id value (system-design § Contracts invariants, the SpecialtyDirectory sentence). A unit test builds the vet's Specialty and the listed Specialty as distinct instances sharing an id.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany on Specialty would create a Vet-Specialty-Vet cycle in the serialized /vets collection and widen eager fetching.
risks.mitigation: Specialty maps no association back to veterinarians (system-design § Contracts invariants). The inversion lives only in SpecialtyDirectory.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory holds mutable entities and lists, which would breach the closed immutability property.
risks.mitigation: Record or final class with List.copyOf defensive copies, and no setters (architecture-principles § Domain Core; the entity exception covers only framework-instantiated types).

risks.risk: The order is unspecified (PRD Open Questions), and a test asserting an order would pin an undecided product choice.
risks.mitigation: Tests assert membership, not sequence. The implementation may return specialties in name order, mirroring PetTypeRepository, as a non-contractual default.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. No ADR: the choices are contained in this slice and follow in-force catalog patterns, so no rule departs from the catalog. SpecialtyRepository is left uncached, so Open Question 5 (vet cache invalidation) is untouched. The 'specialty directory' term is used in the PRD but has no ubiquitous-language entry. Adding it is the product-requirements-expert's call; this is not a foundational trip, since Specialty and Veterinarian are defined.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Exposed surface: the one new endpoint is a read-only GET (SpecialtyController.java:38 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`) that binds no request parameter, path variable, @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody, so it adds no mass-assignment or input-validation surface. It exposes specialty names and veterinarian names, the same data the existing /vets.html already publishes. No new management exposure.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository.java:37 `@Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name")` is a constant JPQL string with no concatenated or request-derived value. It is read-only (`@Transactional(readOnly = true)`, line 36), so it adds no injection path.

Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every data value through escaping `th:text` (line 18 `th:text="${listing.specialtyName}"`, line 21 `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ...}"`). `grep -rn -F 'th:utext' src/main/resources/templates/` returned nothing. The layout's `__${link}__` preprocessing (fragments/layout.html:31) receives only literal menu links, and the new template passes only the literal menu name 'specialties'. No request text reaches expression evaluation.

Unbounded page: listing every specialty with no paging is the PRD's stated requirement (REQ-VET-003 edge case 3). The lookup table is bounded by staff-entered data, not by caller input. VetRepository.findAll is `@Cacheable("vets")`, and Vet specialties load eagerly (Vet.java:47 `@ManyToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)`), so a request triggers at most one uncached specialty query. No caller-controlled amplification.
SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value (List.copyOf on both record components). It performs no I/O, logging, reflection or deserialization, and the singleton controller holds no mutable state.
Secrets sweep: I read the full diff and found no credential, token, key or connection string. There are no new log statements and no exception messages.

Supply chain: the diff changes no dependency (`git status --short build.gradle pom.xml` is empty). OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (`grep -n -F 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle` found nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. From `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`, the resolved versions are Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5.
